unit.title: Everyday idioms (modismos)
unit.subtitle: High-frequency idioms a near-native must recognise

grammar.title: The idioms that make you sound native
grammar.intro: Spanish conversation runs on modismos — fixed idioms whose meaning you cannot deduce word by word. Echar de menos isn't ‘to throw less’, it's ‘to miss’; costar un ojo de la cara isn't about eyes, it's ‘to cost a fortune’. Recognising and using these naturally is what separates a fluent C1 speaker from a merely correct one.

sections.heading: Feelings and reactions
sections.body: These four are everywhere in everyday speech. Note that echar de menos keeps the de, and dar igual / dar lo mismo are interchangeable ways to say ‘it doesn't matter to me’:
conj: to not matter, to not care

ex.en: —Tea or coffee? —I don't mind either way.
ex.note: me da igual = I don't care

sections.heading: Idioms with body parts
sections.body: A whole family of idioms is built on body parts. Learn them as fixed blocks — the article and prepositions don't change (un ojo de la cara, el pelo, la pata):
conj: costar un ojo de la cara
to put one's foot in it

ex.es: Ese reloj cuesta un ojo de la cara.

ex.en: Sorry, I think I put my foot in it.

sections.heading: Time, chance and probability
sections.body: Watch the grammar here: a lo mejor means ‘maybe’ but is followed by the indicative (a lo mejor viene), unlike quizás/tal vez, which allow the subjunctive. Por si acaso = just in case; de repente / de golpe = suddenly:
conj: to pester, to be a nuisance

ex.es: A lo mejor viene mañana, no estoy seguro.
ex.en: Maybe he'll come tomorrow, I'm not sure.
ex.note: a lo mejor + indicative (viene), never subjunctive

ex.en: Take the umbrella, just in case.
ex.note: por si acaso = just in case

takeaways: echar de menos = to miss; dar igual / dar lo mismo = it doesn't matter to you.
estar hecho polvo = worn out; costar un ojo de la cara = to cost a fortune.
tomar el pelo = to pull someone's leg; meter la pata = to put your foot in it; dar la lata = to pester.
a lo mejor takes the INDICATIVE (a lo mejor viene), unlike quizás/tal vez.

mistakes.why: The idiom is echar DE menos; don't drop the de.
a lo mejor is followed by the indicative (viene), not the subjunctive.

mistakes.w: Ese reloj cuesta un ojo de cara.
mistakes.r: Ese reloj cuesta un ojo de la cara.
mistakes.why: The fixed idiom keeps the article: un ojo de la cara.

exercises.prompt: Desde que se mudó a Madrid, lo ___ muchísimo.
exercises.prompt_en: Since he moved to Madrid, I miss him a lot.
exercises.no: ‘To miss’ is echar de menos (with de), not echar menos.

exercises.prompt: ___ viene mañana, pero no estoy nada seguro.
exercises.prompt_en: Maybe he's coming tomorrow, but I'm not at all sure.
exercises.no: ‘Maybe’ + indicative here is a lo mejor; ojalá would force the subjunctive.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Costar un ojo de la cara = to cost a fortune.
exercises.no: The idiom is “cuesta un ojo de la cara” — keep the article la.

exercises.prompt: Llévate una chaqueta, ___ acaso refresca por la noche.
exercises.prompt_en: Take a jacket, just in case it gets chilly at night.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Por si acaso = just in case.
exercises.no: ‘Just in case’ is por si acaso → the missing chunk is “por si”.

exercises.prompt: Match each idiom to its meaning.

exercises.tts: Menos mal que trajiste el paraguas.
accepted: menos mal que trajiste el paraguas
exercises.translation: Thank goodness you brought the umbrella.
exercises.no: It was: “Menos mal que trajiste el paraguas.” (thank goodness that…).

exercises.scenario: A friend swears she's just won the lottery 🎰

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.es: ¡Que he ganado la lotería! ¿No me crees?
lines.en: I've won the lottery! Don't you believe me?

options.text: Venga ya, ¿me estás tomando el pelo?
Venga ya, ¿me estás dando la lata?

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Tomar el pelo = to pull someone's leg.
exercises.no: For ‘are you kidding me?’ use tomar el pelo: “¿me estás tomando el pelo?”

exercises.say: Estoy hecho polvo, me voy a dormir.
exercises.en: I'm exhausted, I'm going to sleep.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Estoy hecho polvo, me voy a dormir.”
